attachment_text:
📄 #cma-mcq-changes-16nov – full questions

1) Wed 18 Nov – Group 1 – Financial Accounting (P6)
Consignment – unsold stock
Q. Goods costing ₹1,00,000 are sent on consignment; the consignor pays freight ₹10,000. One-fourth of the goods remain unsold. The unsold stock is valued at:
A) ₹27,500
B) ₹25,000
C) ₹30,000
D) ₹22,500
✔ Answer: A – Unsold stock = ¼ × (Cost ₹1,00,000 + consignor's freight ₹10,000) = ₹27,500. Expenses that bring the goods to the consignee's place are included.

2) Wed 18 Nov – Group 1 – Cost Accounting (P8)
Operating costing – passenger-km
Q. A bus makes 4 trips a day of 30 km each, carrying 40 passengers on average per trip, for 25 days. Total passenger-km are:
A) 3,000
B) 1,20,000
C) 4,800
D) 30,000
✔ Answer: B – Passenger-km = 30 km × 4 trips × 40 passengers × 25 days = 1,20,000.

3) Thu 19 Nov – Group 1 – Cost Accounting (P8)
Cost Accounting Standards – CAS 1
Q. Which Cost Accounting Standard deals with the classification of cost?
A) CAS 1
B) CAS 4
C) CAS 6
D) CAS 7
✔ Answer: A – CAS 1 covers classification of cost. CAS 4 = cost of production for captive consumption, CAS 6 = material cost, CAS 7 = employee cost.

4) Fri 20 Nov – Group 1 – Cost Accounting (P8)
Rowan premium plan
Q. Time allowed 10 hours, time taken 8 hours, rate ₹50 per hour. Earnings under the Rowan plan are:
A) ₹500
B) ₹480
C) ₹400
D) ₹450
✔ Answer: B – Rowan = TT × R + (TA − TT) ÷ TA × TT × R = 400 + 2/10 × 8 × 50 = ₹480.

5) Sat 21 Nov – Group 1 – Financial Accounting (P6)
AS 2 – costs excluded
Q. Under AS 2, which of these is NOT included in the cost of inventories?
A) Freight inward
B) Conversion costs
C) Selling and distribution costs
D) Purchase price less trade discount
✔ Answer: C – AS 2 excludes selling costs, abnormal wastage, storage (unless needed in production) and administrative overheads not related to production.

6) Fri 4 Dec – Group 2 – Management Accounting (P12)
Shut-down point
Q. Fixed costs ₹2,00,000, of which ₹50,000 will continue even if the plant is shut down. Contribution per unit ₹30. Shut-down point is:
A) 6,667 units
B) 1,667 units
C) 5,000 units
D) 8,333 units
✔ Answer: C – Shut-down point = Fixed costs avoidable by shutting down ÷ Contribution per unit = (2,00,000 − 50,000) ÷ 30 = 5,000 units.

📄 #cma-exam-day-posts – all 16 posts (exam days 10–17 Dec)

── Thu 10 Dec – Group 1 topic – 9:00 AM ──
🍀 ALL THE BEST – P5 Business Laws and Ethics
📅 Today, Thu 10 Dec · 2:00 PM

⚡ Last-minute points
• Valid contract (Sec 10): free consent, competent parties, lawful consideration and object, not expressly declared void.
• Consideration (Sec 2(d)) can be past, present or future, and may move from the promisee or any other person.
• An agreement with a minor is void ab initio (Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose). Necessaries supplied to a minor are paid from the minor's property (Sec 68).
• Unpaid seller's rights against the goods: lien, stoppage in transit and resale.
• Cheque dishonour (Sec 138, NI Act): demand notice within 30 days of the bank's information. The drawer gets 15 days to pay. The complaint is filed within 1 month after that.
• Ethics answers: state the principle, apply it to the facts, then conclude.

✍️ In the exam hall
• Read the whole paper once and plan your order before you start writing.
• Attempt your strongest question first to build confidence.
• Keep 10 minutes at the end to recheck numbers and question numbers.

💪 You have prepared well. Stay calm, read every question twice and write confidently!

── Fri 11 Dec – Group 2 topic – 9:00 AM ──
🍀 ALL THE BEST – P9 Operations Management and Strategic Management
📅 Today, Fri 11 Dec · 2:00 PM

⚡ Last-minute points
• PERT expected time: te = (to + 4tm + tp) ÷ 6. The critical path is the LONGEST path through the network.
• Productivity = output ÷ input. Efficiency = actual output ÷ standard output.
• BCG matrix: Stars (high growth, high share), Cash Cows (low growth, high share), Question Marks (high growth, low share), Dogs (low growth, low share).
• Ansoff: penetration, market development, product development, diversification (riskiest).
• Porter's five forces: new entrants, buyers, suppliers, substitutes and rivalry among existing firms.
• For a case question, name the concept first, then link it to the facts.

✍️ In the exam hall
• Read the whole paper once and plan your order before you start writing.
• Attempt your strongest question first to build confidence.

── Sat 12 Dec – Group 1 topic – 9:00 AM ──
🍀 ALL THE BEST – P6 Financial Accounting
📅 Today, Sat 12 Dec · 2:00 PM

⚡ Last-minute points
• Bill due date = date of bill + term + 3 days of grace. If the due date is a public holiday, it falls on the PRECEDING business day.
• Consignment: unsold stock = cost + proportionate non-recurring expenses (consignor's expenses and consignee's non-recurring expenses).
• Normal loss on consignment is spread over the remaining goods. Abnormal loss is valued like unsold stock and written off.
• BRS: start from one balance and adjust only timing differences and errors. Never adjust both sides for the same item.
• Royalty: short workings are recoupable only within the period allowed by the agreement. Any balance after that is written off.
• Show working notes clearly. Examiners award step marks.

✍️ In the exam hall
• Read the whole paper once and plan your order before you start writing.
• Attempt your strongest question first to build confidence.
• Keep 10 minutes at the end to recheck numbers and question numbers.

── Sun 13 Dec – Group 2 topic – 9:00 AM ──
🍀 ALL THE BEST – P10 Corporate Accounting and Auditing
📅 Today, Sun 13 Dec · 2:00 PM

⚡ Last-minute points
• AS 3 (non-financial company): interest and dividend paid are financing activities, interest and dividend received are investing activities, and income tax is operating unless specifically identified.
• Buy-back: up to 25% of paid-up capital + free reserves, and post buy-back debt-equity not more than 2:1.
• Auditor rotation (Sec 139): an individual can serve 1 term of 5 years and a firm 2 terms of 5 years, followed by a 5-year cooling-off period.
• SA 230: audit documentation is normally retained for at least 7 years from the date of the auditor's report.
• SA 500: external evidence > internal, documentary > oral, originals > copies.
• In Audit, quote the SA or section number with its name. It earns the extra marks.

✍️ In the exam hall

── Mon 14 Dec – Group 1 topic – 9:00 AM ──
🍀 ALL THE BEST – P7 Direct and Indirect Taxation
📅 Today, Mon 14 Dec · 2:00 PM

⚡ Last-minute points
• Default regime (A.Y. 2026-27): income up to ₹4 lakh is nil. Rebate u/s 87A of up to ₹60,000 applies where total income is up to ₹12 lakh (not on special-rate income).
• Standard deduction from salary: ₹75,000 under the default regime and ₹50,000 under the old regime.
• LTCG u/s 112A: 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh. STCG u/s 111A: 20%.
• GST registration threshold: ₹40 lakh for intra-State supply of goods only, ₹20 lakh for services (lower limits in special category States).
• ITC conditions (Sec 16(2)): invoice, receipt of goods or services, tax actually paid to the Government, return filed. Pay the supplier within 180 days or reverse the ITC.
• Write the section number with every adjustment and always state the assessment year.

✍️ In the exam hall
• Read the whole paper once and plan your order before you start writing.

── Tue 15 Dec – Group 2 topic – 9:00 AM ──
🍀 ALL THE BEST – P11 Financial Management and Business Data Analytics
📅 Today, Tue 15 Dec · 2:00 PM

⚡ Last-minute points
• Leverages: DOL = Contribution ÷ EBIT; DFL = EBIT ÷ EBT; DCL = DOL × DFL = Contribution ÷ EBT.
• CAPM: Ke = Rf + β (Rm − Rf). WACC uses market-value weights where available.
• NPV > 0 → accept. PI = PV of inflows ÷ PV of outflows. IRR is the rate at which NPV = 0.
• Operating cycle = raw material + WIP + finished goods + debtors period − creditors period.
• Analytics types: descriptive (what happened), diagnostic (why), predictive (what will happen), prescriptive (what to do).
• Show formula → substitution → answer in every FM computation.

✍️ In the exam hall

── Wed 16 Dec – Group 1 topic – 9:00 AM ──
🍀 ALL THE BEST – P8 Cost Accounting
📅 Today, Wed 16 Dec · 2:00 PM

⚡ Last-minute points
• EOQ = √(2AO ÷ C), where A = annual demand, O = ordering cost per order, C = carrying cost per unit per year.
• Re-order level = maximum usage × maximum lead time. Maximum level = ROL + ROQ − (minimum usage × minimum lead time).
• Halsey (50%) bonus = 50% × time saved × rate. Rowan bonus = (time saved ÷ time allowed) × time taken × rate.
• Process costing: normal loss is absorbed by good units, while abnormal loss and gain are valued at the normal cost per unit.
• Under-absorption and over-absorption of overheads: use a supplementary rate or transfer to Costing P&L, depending on the cause.
• Label every statement (Cost Sheet, Process A/c) exactly as the question asks.

✍️ In the exam hall
• Read the whole paper once and plan your order before you start writing.
• Attempt your strongest question first to build confidence.

── Thu 17 Dec – Group 2 topic – 9:00 AM ──
🍀 ALL THE BEST – P12 Management Accounting
📅 Today, Thu 17 Dec · 2:00 PM

⚡ Last-minute points
• BEP (₹) = Fixed cost ÷ P/V ratio. Margin of safety = Profit ÷ P/V ratio.
• Material cost variance = price variance + usage variance. Usage variance = mix variance + yield variance.
• Labour cost variance = rate variance + efficiency variance (+ idle time variance where given).
• Relevant cost for decisions = future cost that differs between alternatives. Sunk costs are always irrelevant.
• Flexible budget: adjust the budget to the actual activity level before comparing with actuals.
• Mark every variance as (F) or (A). A missing sign loses marks.
